title: Two-Faced Social Agents: Context Collapse in Role-Conditioned Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: Not applicable. The study did not measure any aspect of religion or faith. Its focus was on the ability of large language models to maintain role-conditioned personas based on socioeconomic status (SES) when performing cognitive tasks (SAT math) versus affective preference tasks.
findings: The paper does not contain any findings related to religion. Its key findings relate to 'contextual collapse' where LLMs fail to maintain distinct socioeconomic personas under cognitive load, with models like GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Flash showing uniform optimal performance on SAT math tasks regardless of persona, while Claude Sonnet 4.5 showed limited but measurable (and inverted) SES-based variation. All models could, however, express plausible demographic variation on subjective preference items.
